nodes.name: Ni foam pretreatment
nodes.procedure: Ni foam (1 cm × 2 cm) was soaked in 1.0 M HCl, ethanol, and deionized water for 10 min in turn to remove the impurities of the surface and blown dry before use.
nodes.source_text: Ni foam (1 cm × 2 cm) was soaked in 1.0 M HCl, ethanol, and deionized water for 10 min in turn to remove the impurities of the surface and blown dry before use.

nodes.name: W doped Co-based MOFs synthesis
nodes.procedure: Co(NO3)2·6H2O (1 mmol) and Na2WO4·2H2O (1 mmol) were dissolved in 40 mL deionized water to form aqueous solution A. 2-methylimidazole (16 mmol) was dissolved in 40 mL deionized water to form aqueous solution B. Then, aqueous solution A was poured into aqueous solution B and stirred for several minutes with a piece of pretreated Ni foam. After the solution was placed at room temperature for 1 h, the Ni foam covered with precursor was rinsed with deionized water and ethanol subsequently and dried in vacuum at 60°C overnight.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of W Doped Co-Based MOFs: Co(NO3)2·6H2O (1 mmol) and Na2WO4·2H2O (1 mmol) were dissolved in 40 mL deionized water... dried in vacuum at 60°C overnight.

nodes.name: WS2 growth on MOFs
nodes.procedure: Na2WO4·2H2O (0.011 mmol) and thiourea (0.06 mmol) were added to 15 mL mixed solvent of deionized water (8 mL) and N,N-dimethylformamide (7 mL). Then, the solution was poured into a 100 mL Teflon-lined autoclave with a piece of Ni foam covered with W doped Co-based MOFs precursor. The autoclave was heated at 200°C for 10 h. After reaction, the sample was washed with deionized water and ethanol for several times and dried in vacuum at 60°C overnight.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of WS2@W Doped Co-Based MOFs: Na2WO4·2H2O (0.011 mmol) and thiourea (0.06 mmol)... dried in vacuum at 60°C overnight.

nodes.name: Phosphorization to WS2@W-CoPx
nodes.procedure: WS2@W-CoPx was obtained through the typical phosphatization process. NaH2PO2·H2O (0.20 g) was placed upstream and a piece of Ni foam with WS2@W doped Co-based MOFs was placed downstream in the tubular furnace. The furnace was heated to 300°C with a heating rate of 2°C min^{-1} and kept at 300°C for 1 h under Ar atmosphere.
nodes.source_text: WS2@W-CoPx was obtained through the typical phosphatization process. NaH2PO2·H2O (0.20 g) was placed upstream... under Ar atmosphere.

nodes.name: Oxidation to WS2@W-CoOx
nodes.procedure: WS2@W-CoOx was obtained by the annealing of the Ni foam with WS2@W doped Co-based MOFs at 300°C for 45 min under air.
nodes.source_text: WS2@W-CoOx was obtained by the annealing... at 300°C for 45 min under air.

nodes.name: Carbonization to WS2@W-CoCx
nodes.procedure: The Ni foam with WS2@W doped Co-based MOFs was placed in a tubular furnace under Ar. The furnace was heated to 400°C at a heating rate of 2°C min^-1 and kept at 400°C for 45 min first; and then, it was heated to 800°C at a heating rate of 3°C min^-1 and kept at 800°C for another 60 min.
nodes.source_text: WS2@W-CoCx was obtained by the classical carbonization process... kept at 800°C for another 60 min.

nodes.characterization_summary: WS₂@W-CoPₓ shows red-shifted E¹₂g and A₁g peaks at ≈352 and 420 cm⁻¹ with 65.5 cm⁻¹ separation indicating stronger interfacial coupling and AA/AB stacking compared to other catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectroscopy was first used to characterize the existence of WS₂. As shown in Figure 1a, typical Raman shifts of the E¹₂g in-plane and the A₁g out-of-plane vibration modes of WS₂ can be observed.

properties.description: Overlay of Raman spectra for WS₂-based nanocomposites

nodes.characterization_summary: For WS₂@W-CoPₓ: S 2p₃/₂ 162.3 eV, S 2p₁/₂ 163.4 eV (shifted higher than WS₂); Co 2p Co³⁺ 781.6/797.5 eV, Co²⁺ 783.3/799.0 eV (downshifted 0.4 eV vs W-CoPₓ); W 4f W⁴⁺ 34.3/36.4 eV (downshift >0.7 eV vs W-CoPₓ); P 2p 129.1/129.9/133.9 eV (shifted lower); indicates electron transfer from WS₂ to W-CoPₓ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was then used to evaluate the surface composition and chemical states of the as-prepared catalysts. As shown in Figure 1b, in addition to the elements (Co, W, P, C, N and O) detected in W-CoPₓ, S can also be observed in WS₂@W-CoPₓ.

nodes.characterization_summary: Work functions: WS₂ 3.24 eV, W-CoPₓ 3.32 eV, W-CoOₓ 3.61 eV, W-CoCₓ 3.66 eV; all semiconductors with valence band maximum below Fermi level; electrons transfer from WS₂ to W-CoMₓ (M=P,O,C).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The calculated work functions of WS₂, W-CoPₓ, W-CoOₓ, and W-CoCₓ are 3.24, 3.32, 3.61, and 3.66 eV, respectively.
Finally, the crystal structure of the catalysts was verified by X-ray diffraction (XRD). Figure 1i shows the XRD pattern of WS₂@W-CoPₓ.

nodes.characterization_summary: WS₂@W-CoPₓ shows uniform porous nanosheets with surface bulges; WS₂@W-CoOₓ shows solid nanosheets with short rods; WS₂@W-CoCₓ shows irregular nanoparticle accumulation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) was used to explore the morphology of these as-prepared catalysts.

nodes.characterization_summary: WS₂@W-CoPₓ: WS₂ (006) 0.21 nm, WP (011) 0.29 nm, CoP (211) 0.19 nm; WS₂@W-CoOₓ: WS₂ (006) 0.21 nm, WO₃ (200) 0.37 nm, Co₃O₄ (220) 0.29 nm; WS₂@W-CoCₓ: WS₂ (006) 0.21 nm, WC 0.28 nm, CoC₈ 0.46 nm; confirms atomic-level heterogeneous interfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice spacing of 0.21 nm appeared in the three catalysts was the (006) plane of WS₂. Besides WS₂, the high-resolution TEM (HR-TEM) image of WS₂@W-CoPₓ (Figure 2c) demonstrates two distinct lattice spacings of 0.29 and 0.19 nm...

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS confirms uniform elemental distribution in hybrid catalysts WS₂@W-CoPₓ, WS₂@W-CoOₓ, WS₂@W-CoCₓ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) (Figures S9-S11, Supporting Information) confirms the uniform distribution of elements in the hybrid catalysts.

nodes.characterization_summary: W/Co atomic ratio ≈1:13 in W-doped Co-MOF precursor.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) spectrum (Figure S2, Supporting Information) and the inductive coupled plasma emission spectrometer (ICP) results (Table S1, Supporting Information), the atomic ratios of W/Co are 1:10 and 1:13, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: OER C_dl: WS₂@W-CoPₓ 8.10 mF cm⁻², WS₂@W-CoOₓ 7.63 mF cm⁻², WS₂@W-CoCₓ 2.12 mF cm⁻²; HER C_dl: WS₂@W-CoPₓ 4.05 mF cm⁻², WS₂@W-CoOₓ 2.05 mF cm⁻², WS₂@W-CoCₓ 2.30 mF cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: Mainly due to its porous structure, the calculated C_dl value of WS₂@W-CoPₓ is 8.10 mF cm⁻² which is larger than that of WS₂@W-CoOₓ (7.63 mF cm⁻²) and WS₂@W-CoCₓ (2.12 mF cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: All three catalysts WS₂@W-CoPₓ, WS₂@W-CoOₓ, WS₂@W-CoCₓ show contact angles ≈0° indicating superhydrophilic surfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S12, Supporting Information, the contact angles of the as-prepared WS₂@W-CoPₓ, WS₂@W-CoOₓ, and WS₂@W-CoCₓ are all close to 0° implying that these catalysts are all superhydrophilic.
